title: Model Rule 1.18: Duties to Prospective Client
issuing_body: American Bar Association
propositions: prospective-client status; use and disclosure duties; disqualification framework
limitations: not controlling unless adopted; adopted text and interpretations vary by jurisdiction

title: Formal Opinion 512: Generative Artificial Intelligence Tools
issuing_body: ABA Standing Committee on Ethics and Professional Responsibility
propositions: competence; confidentiality; communication; supervision; candor; fees when lawyers use GAI
limitations: does not create binding nationwide law; addresses GAI generally rather than prospective-client intake specifically

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology
propositions: confabulation; data privacy; information integrity; human-AI configuration; value-chain risks; testing and monitoring
limitations: voluntary and cross-sector; does not state legal-ethics duties

title: AI Companies: Uphold Your Privacy and Confidentiality Commitments
issuing_body: Federal Trade Commission Office of Technology
propositions: AI providers' privacy and confidentiality representations; sensitive customer and end-user data; data-use risk
limitations: not a rule or adjudication and not legal-specific

title: Generative AI Practical Guidance
issuing_body: State Bar of California
propositions: application of competence; confidentiality; communication; candor and related duties to GAI and agentic AI
limitations: California-specific; educational guidance rather than legal advice; replaces 2023 version

title: Opinion 24-1
issuing_body: The Florida Bar
propositions: confidentiality; competence and accuracy; fees; advertising; chatbot use for client intake; disclosure that a prospect is communicating with AI; lawyer responsibility for chatbot communications
limitations: expressly advisory and nonbinding; intake discussion is focused on advertising, disclosure, misleading communications, and screening rather than empirical validation of summarization

title: Formal Opinion 2024-5: Generative AI in the Practice of Law
issuing_body: New York City Bar Association Committee on Professional Ethics
propositions: competence; confidentiality; supervision; disclosure and other duties regarding GAI
limitations: scope and legal effect must not be generalized to all New York or U.S. lawyers

title: Legal Ethics Opinion 1901: Reasonable Fees and the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: Virginia State Bar / Supreme Court of Virginia
propositions: reasonable fees when GAI makes work more efficient
limitations: focused on fees; not prospective-client intake; status changed after its 2025 proposal stage

title: Formal Opinion 2025-6: Ethical Issues Affecting Use of AI to Record Transcribe and Summarize Conversations with Clients
issuing_body: New York City Bar Association Committee on Professional Ethics
propositions: consent; tactical assessment; confidentiality and privilege; accuracy checking for preserved AI summaries
limitations: concerns client conversations rather than web-form prospective-client intake; analogy must be labeled

title: Formal Opinion 510: Avoiding Imputation of a Conflict of Interest When a Law Firm Is Adverse to One of Its Lawyer's Prospective Clients
issuing_body: ABA Standing Committee on Ethics and Professional Responsibility
propositions: prospective-client conflicts and imputation context
limitations: not an AI opinion; full opinion and precise application require acquisition and pinpoint review

title: 2024 Formal Ethics Opinion 1: Use of Artificial Intelligence in a Law Practice
issuing_body: North Carolina State Bar
propositions: competent and secure use; vendor due diligence; supervision; independent judgment; disclosure and billing conditions
limitations: North Carolina-specific; addresses law practice broadly rather than prospective-client intake

title: Ethics Opinion 388: Attorneys' Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Client Matters
issuing_body: District of Columbia Bar Legal Ethics Committee
propositions: technology competence; confidentiality; supervision; client communication; review of output
limitations: District of Columbia-specific; product capabilities and risks may change rapidly; not intake-specific

title: Joint Formal Opinion 2024-200: Ethical Issues Regarding the Use of Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: Pennsylvania Bar Association and Philadelphia Bar Association
propositions: competence; confidentiality; truthfulness; supervision; billing; transparency in AI use
limitations: Pennsylvania-specific; full opinion requires pinpoint acquisition before quotation or final reliance

title: Ethics Opinion KBA E-457: The Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Practice of Law
issuing_body: Kentucky Bar Association
propositions: technology competence; confidentiality; disclosure conditions; fees; court-rule review; firm policies and training
limitations: Kentucky-specific; several propositions concern client matters and court submissions rather than intake

title: 2024 Formal Ethics Opinion 1
issuing_body: North Carolina State Bar
propositions: publicly available AI should generally not receive client-specific information; continuing vendor review; original lawyer responsibility
limitations: the source says generally and as of its date; it does not establish a universal ban

title: Topic: Artificial Intelligence and Legal Ethics — Final White Paper
issuing_body: Arizona Supreme Court Committee on Alternative Business Structures
propositions: identifies client-intake chatbot risks including confidentiality, unintended relationships, unauthorized practice, supervision, and advertising
limitations: not an ethics opinion or binding rule; pre-dates later national and state guidance

title: Massachusetts law about artificial intelligence — attorney ethics 50-state survey links
issuing_body: Massachusetts Trial Court Law Libraries
propositions: collects links to state government and bar attorney-AI guidance
limitations: not primary authority for another jurisdiction; each linked authority must be independently acquired and verified

title: Ethics Opinion RI-392: Access to and Disposition of Client Files After Representation
issuing_body: State Bar of Michigan
propositions: access to lawyer files; return of client property; retention liens after representation
limitations: not an AI opinion and must not support any AI-use claim

title: A Comparative Study of Quality Evaluation Methods for Text Summarization
issuing_body: Nguyen et al.
propositions: evaluates seven summarization models; human evaluation considers clarity accuracy coverage and overall quality; error analysis identifies incompleteness and hallucination
limitations: patent corpus rather than law-firm intake; preprint; does not validate any current vendor or intake configuration

title: Supporting Humans in Evaluating AI Summaries of Legal Depositions
issuing_body: Akter et al.
propositions: source-linked nugget framework surfaces missing unsupported or inaccurate content for human verification
limitations: prototype on nine public civil-deposition transcripts; not an outcome study; not prospective-client intake; uses LLM-based evaluators; industry gift disclosed

title: Challenges to the Monitoring of Deployed AI Systems
issuing_body: NIST Center for AI Standards and Innovation
propositions: post-deployment monitoring categories; human-factor monitoring; monitoring gaps barriers and open questions
limitations: cross-sector and not intake-specific; synthesizes workshops and literature rather than validating a particular monitoring protocol

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework 1.0
issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology
propositions: documentation; accountability; human review; risk measurement and management across lifecycle
limitations: voluntary and cross-sector; does not establish legal duties or product efficacy

title: Automation Bias in AI-Decision Support: Results from an Empirical Study
issuing_body: Kücking et al.
propositions: participants followed erroneous AI recommendations; susceptibility differed by expertise and task conditions
limitations: clinical vignettes rather than legal intake; does not estimate law-firm reviewer behavior; transfer is a design inference only

title: Automation Bias in Mammography: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence BI-RADS Suggestions on Reader Performance
issuing_body: Dratsch et al.
propositions: erroneous AI suggestions adversely affected readers across experience levels in the study setting
limitations: mammography rather than text summarization or legal intake; cannot supply a legal-review error rate

title: Guidance on Web Accessibility and the ADA
issuing_body: U.S. Department of Justice Civil Rights Division
version_or_status: current guidance page; notes 2024 Title II rule separately
propositions: inaccessible forms can prevent accurate submission; labels clear instructions error identification keyboard access and manual testing matter; automated checks alone are insufficient
limitations: informal guidance with no independent binding effect; Title III application and controlling law require matter-specific legal review

title: Michigan Rules of Professional Conduct
issuing_body: Michigan Supreme Court
version_or_status: current compilation updated with orders effective January 1 2026
propositions: Rule 1.18 duties to prospective clients; invited electronic submissions; warnings; limiting initial information collection
limitations: does not validate an AI product or establish summarization efficacy; application remains fact-specific

title: Generative AI: Ethical Best Practices for Lawyers and Judges
issuing_body: Arizona Supreme Court Committee on Artificial Intelligence and the Courts
propositions: competence; confidentiality; supervision; accuracy; prospective-client disclosure when AI is used for intake communications
limitations: not a court rule or ethics opinion; relies in part on authorities from other jurisdictions; does not validate intake summarization performance

title: Ethics Opinion KBA E-457: The Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Practice of Law
issuing_body: Kentucky Bar Association
propositions: technology competence; confidentiality; disclosure conditions; fees; court-rule review; firm policies; supervision and training
limitations: general AI-practice guidance rather than a prospective-client intake opinion; expressly does not address Kentucky advertising rules

title: Idaho Rules of Professional Conduct
issuing_body: Idaho Supreme Court / Idaho State Bar
propositions: Rule 1.18 duties to prospective clients; invited electronic submissions; clear warnings; limited initial collection
limitations: does not validate an AI product or establish summarization efficacy; whether a communication is a consultation depends on the circumstances

title: Office of Professional Conduct: Arkansas Rules of Professional Conduct
issuing_body: Arkansas Judiciary
propositions: identifies the Arkansas Rules of Professional Conduct as current as of June 12 2025
limitations: index page does not itself supply paragraph-level rule text or validate an AI intake product

title: Emily Reed, Respondent Attorney, CPC Docket No. 2025-028
issuing_body: Arkansas Supreme Court Committee on Professional Conduct
propositions: quotes and applies Arkansas Rule 1.18(b) concerning information learned from a prospective client
limitations: decision is matter-specific and does not address AI intake design or all Rule 1.18 comments

title: In re Creation of Arkansas Supreme Court Administrative Order No. 25: Artificial Intelligence
issuing_body: Arkansas Supreme Court
propositions: addresses disclosure of confidential or sealed case information to AI tools; current Judiciary guidance directs court participants to the order
limitations: court-data scope is not private-law-firm prospective-client intake validation
